subject: some help with a tree factor bar graph

messages.author: fca01f44f8b824c4
messages.subject: some help with a tree factor bar graph
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to put together a bar graph that includes two plant species and two ant species as categorical variables and d13C as a dependent variable. I have these variables in two locales. So I would like to have two charts that separates them by locale. I have tried this:

d13<-read.table(file="/Users/paolabarriga/Desktop/fake.txt",header=TRUE,sep="\t")

names(d13)

str(d13)

d13C<-ggplot(d13,aes(x=factor(plant),fill=factor(ant),y=dC,group=locale,colour=ant))+geom_bar(position='dodge')

d13C<-d13C+labs(x="Plant species",y="d13C")

d13C<-d13C+facet_wrap()

d13C


but, the dependent variable is not found. I cannot see what I am doing wrong. If someone can give me a hand, I would be very thankful!

Paola

messages.author: 20c6dbb46920d12c
messages.subject: Re: some help with a tree factor bar graph
parts:
I think you just need to tell it what variable to facet it on:

ggplot(d13,aes(plant,dC,colour=ant,fill=ant))+
geom_bar(position="dodge")+
facet_wrap(~locale)





Adam Loveland

The code does work. It's just that for your data, a bar chart isn't appropriate.

It's hard to know what is appropriate without knowing more about what you're trying to learn, but something along the lines of a boxplot or pointrange may be a more appropriate choice:

ggplot(d13,aes(plant,dC,colour=ant,fill=ant))+geom_boxplot()+ facet_wrap(~locale)

Adam Loveland
